docs.title: credforge
docs.text:
Check a credential registry against the places it describes, without reading a single value.

A registry such as systemspec-credential says which credentials should exist, where each is stored, who uses it and how it rotates. credforge observes the stores and consumers themselves (a repository's Actions secrets and the secrets its workflows read, a parameter store's names) and reports where they disagree with the registry and its event log: the secret a workflow needs that was never set, the token regenerated at the issuer but never updated in one repository, the value changed with nothing recorded.

Status: v0.1.0 checks and records; it never writes a value. Installing and rotating values through OmniVault providers follows. See the roadmap.

docs.title: What it reports
docs.text: State Meaning missing A listed store does not hold the credential stale A store was set before the credential's current value was made unregistered A workflow reads a secret the registry stores nowhere it can be read changed A store was set after the log's latest event, with nothing recorded unrecorded A store holds a credential the log has no event for unlisted A store holds a name no credential in use names unobserved No binding reaches the store present As recorded

docs.title: Install
docs.text: go install github.com/plexusone/credforge/cmd/credforge@latest

docs.title: Use
docs.text:
Beside the registry and its event log, write a targets file that says how each store is reached. It holds no secrets:

{
  "formatVersion": "1",
  "bindings": [
    { "store": "github-actions", "account": "example-org/*", "github": {} },
    { "store": "aws-ssm", "account": "hosting", "aws": { "profile": "hosting", "region": "us-west-2" } }
  ],
  "scan": { "githubRepositories": ["example-org/web", "example-org/api"] }
}

Then check:

export GITHUB_TOKEN=$(gh auth token)
credforge check --registry credentials.json --events events.json --targets targets.json

listed 3 scope(s): 0 missing, 1 stale, 1 unregistered, 0 changed, 1 unrecorded, 1 unlisted, 1 unobserved, 0 present
stale         app/ci/deploy  github-actions:example-org/web:DEPLOY_TOKEN  set 2026-03-01, before the current value was made on 2026-03-11
unregistered  -              github-actions:example-org/api:DEPLOY_TOKEN  a consumer reads this name, and no credential stores it here (.github/workflows/ci.yaml)
unrecorded    app/prod/DB    aws-ssm:hosting:/app/prod/DB                 set 2026-03-01; the log has no event for it
unlisted      -              aws-ssm:hosting:/app/prod/OLD                no credential stores this name
Flag What it does --record Logs unrecorded stores as created and changed ones as deployed --fail-on States that make the exit status 1; default missing,stale,unregistered --include-planned Also compares planned credentials --only Compares only credentials whose ID matches a pattern, such as 'app/prod/*' --grace How far a store's change and the log's event may differ; default 24h --format text or json --all Lists present and unobserved stores, not only their counts

The exit status is 0 when nothing is in a --fail-on state, 1 when something is, and 2 on an error.

docs.title: Connectors
docs.text: Store What is listed Never called GitHub Actions secrets (github-actions) Repository secret names and when each was set; workflow files' secrets.NAME Secret values cannot be read through GitHub's API AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store (aws-ssm) Parameter names and last change, one directory level at a time GetParameter, GetParameters

docs.title: In Go
docs.text:
The comparison is a pure function, and the command tree mounts in a host tool that builds its registry in Go:

cmd := cli.New(cli.Options{
    Use:      "observe",
    Registry: buildRegistry,                       // func() (*credspec.Registry, error)
    Targets:  func() (*targets.File, error) { return myTargets, nil },
})

rep := credforge.Compare(reg, log, scopes, observations, references, credforge.Options{
    Grace: credforge.DefaultGrace,
})
events, err := credforge.Record(reg, log, rep, credforge.DefaultGrace)

docs.title: Install
docs.text: go install github.com/plexusone/credforge/cmd/credforge@latest

docs.title: What you need
docs.text:
• A credential registry and its event log in systemspec-credential's format. Each credential lists its stores by type, account and path, such as github-actions, example-org/web, DEPLOY_TOKEN.
  • Read access to the stores: a GitHub token that can read the repositories' Actions secrets and contents, and AWS credentials that may call ssm:DescribeParameters.

docs.title: Write a targets file
docs.text:
The targets file binds each store type and account the registry names to a connection. It holds no secrets: a GitHub binding names the environment variable with the token, and an AWS binding names a profile and region.

{
  "formatVersion": "1",
  "bindings": [
    { "store": "github-actions", "account": "example-org/*", "github": { "tokenEnv": "GITHUB_TOKEN" } },
    { "store": "aws-ssm", "account": "hosting", "aws": { "profile": "hosting", "region": "us-west-2" } }
  ],
  "scan": { "githubRepositories": ["example-org/web", "example-org/api"] }
}
  • account matches the registry store's account exactly, or as a pattern such as example-org/*; * matches any. The first matching binding wins.
  • A store no binding reaches is unobserved, never missing.
  • scan.githubRepositories lists repositories to check even when the registry stores nothing there, so a workflow that reads an unknown secret is found.

credforge schema targets prints the file's JSON Schema.

docs.title: Check
docs.text:
export GITHUB_TOKEN=$(gh auth token)
credforge check --registry credentials.json --events events.json --targets targets.json

Read the findings from the top: missing, stale and unregistered are things that break builds and deploys; changed and unrecorded are gaps in the log; unlisted are names the registry does not know.

docs.title: Record
docs.text:
credforge check --record --fail-on ''

Logs each unrecorded store as created and each changed one as deployed, at the time the store reports, by credforge. The registry is never edited.

docs.title: In CI
docs.text: Run credforge check on a schedule with a read-only token; the default --fail-on missing,stale,unregistered fails the job when something would break.

docs.title: v0.1.0
docs.text: Release Date: 2026-11-20

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
• Check a credential registry against reality. credforge check compares a systemspec-credential registry and its event log with the stores and consumers it names, and reports each store as missing, stale, unregistered, changed, unrecorded, unlisted, unobserved or present.
  • No value is ever read. Observers list names and when each was last set; no type has a field for a value, and the AWS observer never calls GetParameter.
  • Catches what breaks builds. A workflow reading a secret its repository never had is unregistered; a store last set before the credential's rotation is stale.
  • Records what it sees. --record logs unrecorded stores as created and changed ones as deployed, so the event log and the rotation calendar catch up with the stores.

docs.title: Status
docs.text: v0.1.0 is read-only. Organization and environment secrets, issuer observations such as a token's expiry, and installing and rotating values through OmniVault providers follow; the roadmap lists them.

docs.title: Comparison
docs.text:
Compare is a pure function over the registry, the log and what was observed. For each active credential's primary and rendered stores:

State When unobserved No listed scope covers the store missing A listed scope does not hold it, and the credential is not tagged optional unrecorded Held, and the log has no created, rotated or deployed event stale Set more than the grace before the latest created or rotated event changed Set more than the grace after the latest created, rotated or deployed event present Otherwise

Names no credential in use stores are unlisted, including those only a retired credential stores. A name a consumer reads and no credential stores is unregistered; a GitHub organization secret satisfies a repository's reference. The grace, a day by default, absorbs the time between changing a value and recording it.

docs.title: Connectors
docs.text: Package Observes github A repository's Actions secret names and updated_at; its workflows' secrets.NAME and secrets['NAME'] references awsssm Parameter Store names and last change, one directory level at a time, with DescribeParameters

docs.title: Targets file
docs.text: A JSON file, with a schema generated from the Go types, binds each store type and account the registry names to a connection: a GitHub token's environment variable and API URL, or an AWS profile and region. It holds no secrets. Stores no binding reaches are unobserved, not missing.

docs.title: Command line
docs.text: credforge check writes text or JSON, records with --record, filters with --only and --include-planned, and exits 1 on --fail-on states (default missing,stale,unregistered) and 2 on errors. credforge schema targets prints the targets schema. cli.New mounts the same commands in a host tool that builds its registry and targets file in Go.

docs.title: PLAN: credforge
docs.text: Initiative: INIT-CREDFORGE-001

docs.title: Order
docs.text:
1. Core first (RMI-CREDFORGE-001, -002). Compare and Record are pure and carry every rule, so they are written and tested against fixtures before any connector exists.
  2. Targets (RMI-CREDFORGE-003), since Check derives its scopes from it.
  3. Connectors (RMI-CREDFORGE-004, -005), each behind its interface and tested against fakes.
  4. Command line (RMI-CREDFORGE-006), then a check against a real registry before the first release.
  5. Release v0.1.0 and make the repository public: README, MkDocs site, CHANGELOG, CI, and a clean publication scan. The repository stays private until Phase 1 works end to end; it is not published with specs alone.
  6. Phases 2 to 4 follow, in order, each released on its own.

docs.title: Adoption
docs.text: A host tool that already builds a credential registry in Go mounts cli.New beside credspec's commands, binds its stores in a targets file, and replaces any per-store comparison of its own with credforge check.

docs.title: Risks
docs.text: Risk Mitigation A connector reads a value by mistake Only listing endpoints are called; tests assert the value endpoints are never hit stale and changed misfire when events are recorded late The grace window, a flag, defaulting to 24 hours Registry store accounts are free text Bindings match accounts exactly or by pattern; unmatched stores are unobserved, never missing Organization and environment secrets satisfy references in Phase 1 only partly Organization secrets count when the registry stores them at the owner; the rest arrives in Phase 2 GitHub rate limits on large fleets One listing per repository, paged; workflow files fetched once per run

docs.title: Definition of done (Phase 1)
docs.text:
• go test ./... and golangci-lint run pass; coverage reported.
  • credforge check run against a real registry with GitHub and SSM bindings reports the drift it contains, and --record writes events that credspec validate accepts.
  • README, docs site, CHANGELOG and release notes for v0.1.0.

docs.title: PRD: credforge — check and act on a credential registry
docs.text: Initiative: INIT-CREDFORGE-001 Status: proposed

docs.title: Problem
docs.text:
A team that runs a few hosted apps soon holds dozens of credentials: deploy-time secrets in a cloud parameter store, CI tokens in GitHub Actions, OAuth client secrets, API keys for analytics and DNS providers, root keys kept offline. A registry without values, such as systemspec-credential, says what should exist, where each value is kept, who uses it and how it rotates, and an event log says what happened to it.

A registry is only as good as its last edit. Nothing compares it with the places it describes, so it drifts, and the drift is found when something breaks:

  • A CI token is regenerated at the issuer. One repository's secret is updated; another keeps the revoked value, and its builds fail days later.
  • A workflow starts reading a secret the registry does not list for that repository, and the repository never had it set.
  • A token's access is widened at the issuer, or not widened when a new private dependency arrives, and the registry's entitlements no longer say what the token can do.
  • A secret is changed in a store and nobody records it, so the rotation calendar is wrong.

Each of these is visible from the stores and issuers themselves, without reading a single value: a secret's name and when it was last set, a workflow file's secrets.NAME references, a parameter's last-modified time.

docs.title: Goal
docs.text: credforge reads a credential registry and its event log, observes the stores, issuers and consumers it names, and reports where they disagree. It records what it observes as events. Later it installs and rotates values, taking them from a master copy through OmniVault providers and writing them to every store the registry lists.

docs.title: Users
docs.text:
• An operator who keeps a registry for a small fleet and wants one command that says what is missing, stale or unrecorded before a deploy or a release.
  • A host tool, such as a deployment CLI, that already builds a registry in Go and mounts credforge's commands over it.
  • CI, running the check on a schedule and failing when drift appears.

docs.title: Phase 1: observe and compare (read-only)
docs.text:
1. Never read a value. Observers list names, dates and metadata only. No type has a field for a value. A connector that cannot list without reading values is not written.
  2. Compare a registry with stores. For each active credential and each of its stores credforge can observe, report one of:
  3. present: the store holds it;
  4. missing: the store does not;
  5. stale: the store was last set before the credential's latest created or rotated event, so it holds an earlier value;
  6. changed: the store was set after the latest event, and nothing recorded why;
  7. unrecorded: present, and the log has no event for it at all.
  8. Report what the registry does not know. Names in an observed scope (a repository's Actions secrets, a parameter directory) that no credential names are unlisted.
  9. Check consumers against stores. A GitHub workflow that references secrets.NAME in a repository where the registry stores no NAME is unregistered. This finds the secret a workflow needs before CI does.
  10. Record observations. With --record, an unrecorded present store is logged as created, and a changed store as deployed, at the time the store reports, by credforge. The registry is never edited.
  11. Connect by binding, not by guessing. A small targets file binds each store type and account in the registry to how it is reached (an AWS profile and region, a GitHub token's environment variable). A store without a binding is reported as unobserved, not as missing.
  12. First connectors: GitHub Actions repository secrets, GitHub workflow files, and AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store.
  13. A gate. credforge check exits non-zero when any finding is in the states chosen with --fail-on (default missing,stale,unregistered).
  14. Embeddable. The command line is a Cobra command a host tool mounts over a registry it builds itself, as systemspec-credential's is.

docs.title: Phase 2: more of the world
docs.text:
1. GitHub organization and environment secrets, with the repositories an organization secret is shared with.
  2. Issuer observations: the expiry and repository access of fine-grained personal access tokens granted to an organization, compared with the registry's entitlements and expiry events.
  3. Scheduled checks in CI, with a report artifact.

docs.title: Phase 3: install and rotate
docs.text:
1. Push. Write a value from a master copy, named by an OmniVault URI (op://…, aws-sm://…, keyring://…), to each store the registry lists for that credential, then record deployed per store.
  2. Rotate. For credentials the operator generates (random secrets, key pairs), make a new value in memory, write it to the master copy and every store, and record rotated. Issuer-made credentials print the issuer step and then push.
  3. Plans first. Every write runs as a plan that lists each store it would change and asks before applying. --dry-run only prints it.

docs.title: Phase 4: frameworks
docs.text:
1. An app framework can declare the credentials an app reads, so credforge checks an app's configuration against the registry.
  2. A connections library that stores tenants' credentials can report their metadata (names, issuer, last rotation) as observations, never values.

docs.title: Non-goals
docs.text:
• Storing values. credforge keeps none; master copies stay in the vaults OmniVault reaches.
  • Replacing the registry format. systemspec-credential owns the schema, the event log, the lifecycle state and the reports.
  • Runtime secret access inside apps. That is OmniVault's and VaultGuard's.
  • Key management. Encryption key lifecycles are KeyForge's.

docs.title: Success measures
docs.text:
• Each drift above is reported by credforge check before it breaks a build or a deploy.
  • A fleet's GitHub and parameter-store credentials are checked in one command, with no value leaving its store.
  • After Phase 3, rotating a CI token is one issuer step and one command.

docs.title: TRD: credforge — check and act on a credential registry
docs.text: Initiative: INIT-CREDFORGE-001 Status: proposed

docs.title: Boundaries
docs.text:
Concern Owner Registry, event log, lifecycle state, reports github.com/plexusone/systemspec-credential (credspec) Observing stores, issuers and consumers; comparing; recording; later writing values credforge Reading and writing values in vaults github.com/plexusone/omnivault and its provider modules Encryption key lifecycle inside an app github.com/plexusone/keyforge

credforge imports credspec and never redefines its types. It adds no field for a value to any type, as credspec does not.

docs.title: Packages
docs.text:
credforge/            core: keys, scopes, observations, references, findings, Compare, Check
credforge/targets     the targets file: binding store types and accounts to connections
credforge/github      observers for GitHub Actions secrets and workflow references
credforge/awsssm      observer for AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store
credforge/cli         the embeddable Cobra command tree
cmd/credforge         the standalone binary

The core package depends on the standard library and credspec only. Connectors live in their own packages so the core stays small; they may move to separate modules if their dependencies grow.

docs.title: Core model
docs.text:
// Key names one place a value is kept: a store type, an account at that
// store (a repository, an AWS account) and a path (a secret name, a
// parameter name). It matches credspec.Store's Type, Account and Path.
type Key struct{ Type, Account, Path string }

// Scope is a listing: every name under Prefix in one account of one store
// type. An empty Prefix is the whole account.
type Scope struct{ Type, Account, Prefix string }

// Observation is one name a store reported, with when it was last set.
// It never carries a value.
type Observation struct {
    Key
    Modified time.Time
}

// Reference is a consumer naming a value it reads, such as a workflow's
// `secrets.NAME`: Key is where the consumer expects it.
type Reference struct {
    Key
    Source string // the file or component that reads it
}

// Observer lists one store type's names in a scope.
type Observer interface {
    Observe(ctx context.Context, s Scope) ([]Observation, error)
}

// ReferenceFinder lists the references consumers in one account make.
type ReferenceFinder interface {
    References(ctx context.Context, account string) ([]Reference, error)
}

docs.title: Findings
docs.text:
type State string // present, missing, stale, changed, unrecorded, unlisted, unregistered, unobserved

type Finding struct {
    State      State
    Credential string       // empty for unlisted
    Store      Key
    Modified   *time.Time   // when the store last set it, when observed
    Source     string       // the consumer, for unregistered
    Detail     string
}

Compare(reg, log, scopes, observations, references, opts) Report is a pure function: it does no I/O, so every rule is unit-tested with fixtures.

Rules, for each credential whose status is active (and planned with IncludePlanned), and each store whose role is primary or rendered:

  1. The store's key is in no observed scope: unobserved. Nothing is inferred about it.
  2. The key is in an observed scope and not observed: missing, unless the credential is tagged optional.
  3. Observed, and the log has no created, rotated or deployed event for the credential: unrecorded.
  4. Observed, and Modified is earlier than the latest created or rotated event by more than Grace (default 24 hours): stale. The store holds a value made before the current one.
  5. Observed, and Modified is later than the latest created, rotated or deployed event by more than Grace: changed.
  6. Otherwise present.

Then, for every observed name no credential's store names: unlisted. For every reference whose key no credential's store names: unregistered. A GitHub reference is also satisfied by a github-actions store whose account is the repository's owner (an organization secret).

Grace absorbs the order operators work in: regenerate, install, then record, which puts the event a little after the store's change.

docs.title: Recording
docs.text: Record(reg, log, report, now) ([]credspec.Event, error) appends, for each unrecorded finding, a created event, and for each changed finding a deployed event, at the store's Modified time, by: credforge, with a note naming the store. It never edits the registry. The caller saves the log.

docs.title: Check
docs.text:
type Checker struct {
    Observers  map[string]Observer        // by store type
    References map[string]ReferenceFinder // by store type
    Targets    *targets.File
}

func (c *Checker) Check(ctx context.Context, reg *credspec.Registry, log *credspec.Log, opts Options) (Report, error)

Check derives the scopes from the registry and the targets file, calls the observers, and passes everything to Compare:

  • github-actions: one scope per distinct account (owner/repo) among the registry's stores, plus each repository the targets file lists for scanning. Workflow references are read for the same repositories.
  • aws-ssm: one scope per directory of each stored parameter name (the path up to its last /), listed one level deep, so a parameter beside a registered one and not in the registry is unlisted.

A store type or account without a binding produces no scope, so its stores are unobserved. An observer's error is returned with the scope it was listing; a partial report is never presented as complete.

docs.title: Targets file
docs.text:
A small JSON file (camelCase, schema generated from the Go types) beside the registry. It holds no secrets: only how to reach each store.

{
  "formatVersion": "1",
  "bindings": [
    { "store": "github-actions", "account": "*", "github": { "tokenEnv": "GITHUB_TOKEN" } },
    { "store": "aws-ssm", "account": "hosting (us-west-2)", "aws": { "profile": "hosting", "region": "us-west-2" } }
  ],
  "scan": { "githubRepositories": ["example-org/web-app", "example-org/api"] }
}

account matches a store's account exactly or as a path.Match pattern; the first match wins. A host tool may build the file in Go instead.

docs.title: GitHub (credforge/github)
docs.text:
• Actions secrets: GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/secrets, paged. It returns each secret's name, created_at and updated_at, never a value. Modified is updated_at.
  • Workflow references: GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/contents/.github/workflows and each .yml or .yaml file's raw content from the default branch. References are secrets.NAME and secrets['NAME']; GITHUB_TOKEN is skipped. secrets: inherit into a reusable workflow is noted, not followed, in Phase 1.
  • Plain net/http with a token from the binding's environment variable (default GITHUB_TOKEN, then GH_TOKEN), and a configurable base URL for tests and GitHub Enterprise Server. The token needs read access to the repositories' Actions secrets and contents.

docs.title: AWS SSM (credforge/awsssm)
docs.text:
• DescribeParameters with a Path filter, OneLevel, paged. It returns names and LastModifiedDate, never values. GetParameter is never called.
  • The binding names the profile and region; the AWS SDK's default chain supplies credentials.

docs.title: Command line
docs.text:
credforge check   --registry credentials.json --events events.json --targets targets.json
                  [--record] [--fail-on missing,stale,unregistered] [--include-planned]
                  [--grace 24h] [--only <id-pattern>] [--format text|json]
credforge schema  targets

Text output groups findings by state, worst first, one line each, naming the credential, the store and the date; --format json writes the report. The exit status is 1 when any finding is in a --fail-on state, 2 on a usage or connection error.

cli.New(cli.Options{...}) returns the tree; like credspec's, its Options.Registry lets a host tool supply a registry built in Go, and Options.Targets a targets file built in Go.

docs.title: Phase 3 design notes (writes)
docs.text:
• Destination is the write side of a store type: Set(ctx, Key, value). GitHub Actions secrets are written sealed with the repository's public key (libsodium sealed box); SSM parameters as SecureString.
  • The master copy is named by an OmniVault URI on the credential (a tag or the targets file, not a value), read once into memory, written to each store, then zeroed where the language allows.
  • Every write is a plan first. Nothing writes without --apply and a confirmation, or --yes in CI.

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
• No value is read in Phases 1 and 2. Tests assert no observer calls a value-returning endpoint (GetParameter, GetSecretValue, secret contents).
  • Tokens are read from the environment, never from flags, and never printed or logged; HTTP errors are reported without request headers.
  • The targets file and reports contain names, accounts and dates. They are as sensitive as the registry and belong wherever it is kept.

docs.title: Testing
docs.text:
• Compare and Record: table tests for every rule, including grace edges, optional and planned credentials, organization secrets and multiple stores per credential.
  • Connectors: httptest servers for GitHub; an interface over the SSM client's DescribeParameters for AWS. No live calls in unit tests; an opt-in live test reads one repository when a token is set.
  • CLI: golden output for text and JSON, exit codes, and --record writing the expected events.
